cells.tense: The care is moving through you now and it isn't draining you.
cells.act: release it on purpose, not by losing it
cells.ask: Name something you've been holding for a person or a project that's found its feet, and set it down on purpose. Say it's finished, then leave it a day and watch what your hands reach for.
cells.core:
Pattern, done well, looks like providing conditions and stepping back to let them do their work. That's what's happening: something is growing because you're not standing on it. Your hands stay open, and because they do, the thing actually develops rather than being propped up.

Something in this has finished and hasn't been let go of. You know which one, probably. Set it down on purpose — not dropped, not lost, released with you awake to it. Then leave it for a day. What remains is the part still growing, and with your hands free you can feel the difference between tending and hauling.
cells.sheetLine: What you tend is growing, and your hands are open.
cells.place: where the whole pattern is visible

cells.tense: You will be bracing toward a future you're already arranging, and the care is tightening.
cells.act: move through the fog without demanding the map
cells.ask: Take a single step with only enough light to see that step. Walk it done and leave tomorrow's stretch of the path dark.
cells.core:
Two versions of this are running at once — the one that's actually unfolding and the one you've already scripted. You keep nudging the real thing toward the scripted one. From where you sit, that reads as care. From the other end it reads as hands.

Picture the outcome a year on, turned out fine. You can do that, and the picture will be accurate — it tends to be. The trap is stepping back into today and arranging today to match it. So take a step without needing the rest of the path. One step, enough light, done. The rest stays unknown until you're standing there. That's not abandoning anyone; it's putting the outcome down where it belongs and picking your feet back up.
cells.sheetLine: The next step is enough to take.

cells.tense: Nothing was growing for a long while, and you kept standing at a door that had already closed.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Keep a lamp lit for something you want this week — one want, not a plan — and let turning toward it be the whole practice.
cells.core:
Some of what you do — reading a room, giving everyone the missing piece — is genuinely good. It's also true that nothing of your own has come up through it. The block isn't idleness. Nobody has been asking what you'd reach for.

There's a want that went quiet and hasn't been asked back. Keep a lamp lit for it this week — one want, not a plan — and let turning toward it be the whole practice. It doesn't have to be a project. It doesn't have to be useful to anyone. Let it be plain, at least to you. That want is allowed to be yours, and so is the time it takes to notice it again.
cells.sheetLine: There's something you want. Turn toward it.

cells.tense: You are carrying out care in a room where the choice of it went missing a while back.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: Leave your hands empty for one breath before you take the next thing on. Set it down first; pick it up only if you mean to.
cells.core:
Certain things happen before you've decided whether to do them. You notice, you smooth it over, you carry it. The work is real. It also costs you, and the cost has been filed under 'that's just how I am' rather than under any choice you're making.

That's the whole problem — not too much care, care running with no one visibly at the wheel. Before the next thing, leave your hands empty for one breath. Set it down first. Then pick it up only if you mean to. If you do, you'll be picking, not being picked by it. The work goes on. It just has someone standing beside it who knows they're there.
cells.sheetLine: The care is yours. You can name it so.

attempts.check: The claim 'others experience you as caretaker while you feel depleted' in Unacknowledged is the record's own, but I cannot claim the person never chose the roles or that they were pushed; I can only point to the depletion and the unrecognised authorship. The reader could reasonably say the roles were chosen and wanted, and the depletion is ordinary tiredness; the ask survives that because pausing before an act of care still shows them the author even if the account is wrong. The sentence that serves me rather than them is any hint that the care is 'too much' or that others should feel guilty; I've cut all of that. I checked each ask against the act list word-for-word: act 1 is 'release it on purpose, not by losing it'; act 2 is 'move through the fog without demanding the map'; act 3 is 'move toward the thing you actually want'; act 4 is 'put it down and leave your hands empty a while'. Each is small enough to be done without anyone else, and each opens on a different verb.
